# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Account Lockout

Locks an account for 15 minutes after ten failed sign-in attempts, including that of the built-in administrator, and puts the device into BitLocker recovery after ten failed attempts.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | CIS v4 Windows 11 L1 and the Microsoft Security Baseline — values verified against Policy CSP DeviceLock (AccountLockoutPolicy, AllowAdministratorLockout) and LocalPoliciesSecurityOptions. |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Account_Lockout.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Account_Lockout.json) |

> Threshold 10 and not 5: at 5 a user who makes a mistake locks themselves out too easily, and 10 is the value of the Microsoft Security Baseline. The account lockout lifts itself after 15 minutes — nobody needs to be called for that. The machine threshold (InteractiveLogon MachineAccountLockoutThreshold) does something else: it puts the device into BitLocker recovery after ten failed attempts, and then the recovery key is needed. That is intended for a stolen laptop, not for a forgetful user, but expect the occasional helpdesk request. AccountLockoutPolicy requires Windows 11 22H2 with KB5053657 or 24H2; older devices silently ignore the setting. NOTE: IntuneAdmin sets this setting in its NIS2 profile to the bare value "15" — the CSP expects the three fields as one string ("AccountLockoutDuration:15, AccountLockoutThreshold:10, ResetAccountLockoutCounterAfter:15"), so that value is broken there. Do not copy it.
